definition_zh: 教育的；与教育相关的；有教育意义的；用于教学的；教育机构的；受教育程度的；教育技术的；教育心理与教育不平等的
definition_en: relating to education or to teaching, or serving to instruct and improve knowledge
core_image: 一位老师在黑板上把一道线拉长，学生顺着这条线自己走到了没教过的地方
scene: 课堂上黑板已经写满，老师却仍在往边上添新的一行。The teacher keeps writing past the filled board, and that habit makes every lesson deeply educational.
sceneCN: 这里 educational 是「有教育意义的、能教人的」（第 2 个义项：有教育意义的）；句意：老师把线延长到尚未讲过的地方，让学生顺着走进去，这是最有教育意义的做法。图中可辨识物件：黑板、延长的粉笔线、学生的手、未擦净的旧字、打开的课本。

pos.zh: 教育的；教育性的；有教育意义的

senses.title: Of education: belonging to the institution
senses.titleCN: 教育的：属于教育制度的
senses.definition: relating to the system, institutions, or process of education
senses.definitionCN: 与教育制度、机构或过程相关的
senses.example: The country spends a small share of its budget on educational infrastructure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家把预算中很小的一部分用于教育基础设施。
senses.why: Educational is education plus -al. Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'bring up'. The adjective simply marks what belongs to that process.
senses.whyCN: educational 是 education 加 -al。education 出自拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”，源于 educare“抚养”。这个形容词只是标记“属于这一过程的东西”。

senses.title: Instructive: able to teach something
senses.titleCN: 有教育意义的：能教给人东西
senses.definition: providing knowledge or moral improvement, often outside a classroom
senses.definitionCN: 提供知识或道德提升，且常发生在课堂之外
senses.example: The failure was more educational than the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败比那堂课更有教育意义。
senses.why: Here -al shifts from 'belonging to education' to 'having the effect of teaching'. A museum, a mistake, or a game can be educational without being part of a school.
senses.whyCN: 这里 -al 从“属于教育”转为“具有教导效果”。博物馆、一次失误、一个游戏都可以是 educational，而不属于学校。

senses.title: For teaching: materials made to instruct
senses.titleCN: 用于教学：为教而造的材料
senses.definition: designed or used for teaching, as in educational books, games, or software
senses.definitionCN: 为教学而设计或使用的，如教育书籍、游戏或软件
senses.example: The app was marketed as educational but taught little.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用以教育为卖点，却几乎没教什么。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a market category: educational toys promise instruction as a product feature. The word now describes intent rather than result.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词成了市场类别：教育玩具把“教导”当作产品卖点。此时它描述“意图”，而非“结果”。

senses.title: Of attainment: how far schooling went
senses.titleCN: 受教育程度：上到哪一级
senses.definition: concerning the level of schooling a person or group has completed
senses.definitionCN: 关于个人或群体完成的教育层级
senses.example: Educational attainment predicts income more strongly than birthplace.
senses.exampleCN: 受教育程度对收入的预测力比出生地更强。
senses.why: Statistics turns a process into a level. 'Educational attainment' counts years and certificates, which is a measurable proxy for what the process gave.
senses.whyCN: 统计把过程变成一个层级。“受教育程度”计年数与证书，作为该过程所给之物的可测代理。

senses.title: Of technology: tools built for learning
senses.titleCN: 教育技术的：为学习而造的工具
senses.definition: relating to digital or mechanical tools used to support teaching and learning
senses.definitionCN: 与支持教与学的数字或机械工具相关的
senses.example: Educational technology promised personalisation and delivered screens.
senses.exampleCN: 教育技术承诺个性化，交付的却是屏幕。
senses.why: The compound 'educational technology' treats teaching as a field that can be engineered. The adjective keeps its institutional sense but attaches to machines.
senses.whyCN: 复合词 educational technology 把教学当作可被工程化的领域。形容词保持其制度义，却接到了机器上。

senses.title: Of psychology: learning as a subject of study
senses.titleCN: 教育心理的：把学习当作研究对象
senses.definition: concerning the psychological study of learning, motivation, and instruction
senses.definitionCN: 关于学习、动机与教学心理研究的
senses.example: Educational psychology studies how feedback changes retention.
senses.exampleCN: 教育心理学研究反馈如何改变记忆保持。
senses.why: A discipline name built on the adjective means 'the psychology of education'. The word marks the application of one field to the concerns of another.
senses.whyCN: 以这个形容词构成的学科名，意为“教育过程的心理学”。这个词标记一个领域对另一个领域的应用。

senses.title: Of inequality: gaps in what schooling delivers
senses.titleCN: 教育不平等的： schooling 所给之物的差距
senses.definition: concerning differences in access, resources, or outcomes among groups
senses.definitionCN: 关于不同群体在入学机会、资源或结果上的差异
senses.example: Educational inequality persists even when funding is equalised.
senses.exampleCN: 即使经费拉平，教育不平等依然存在。
senses.why: The adjective allows policy to name the arena of a gap without naming its cause. 'Educational inequality' locates the difference in outcomes, not in genes or income.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让政策能说出差距所在的场域，而不必说出原因。“教育不平等”把差异定位在结果上，而不在基因或收入上。

senses.title: Of value: what a thing teaches
senses.titleCN: 教育价值：一物能教什么
senses.definition: the worth of an experience or object measured by what it teaches
senses.definitionCN: 按“能教什么”来衡量一段经历或一个物件的价值
senses.example: The documentary's educational value outweighed its inaccuracies.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片的教益超过了它的失实之处。
senses.why: Value language asks for a return: what did the learner get? Educational value is the pedagogy of an object, whether or not anyone planned it.
senses.whyCN: 价值语言要求回报：学习者得到了什么？教育价值就是一个物件的“教学性”，无论是否有人刻意设计。

intro.en: Educational is education plus -al. Education entered English in the 16th century from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'bring up, rear'. educare is related to educere 'lead out', and the old 'drawing out' idea is often mentioned, though the direct source is educare rather than educere.
intro.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al。education 于 16 世纪经拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”进入英语，源于 educare“抚养、培育”。educare 与 educere“引出”相关，“把潜能引出来”的旧说常被提及，但直接来源是 educare，而非 educere。

items.en: Educational psychology, educational technology and educational inequality become established compound terms in research and policy.
items.cn: 教育心理学、教育技术、教育不平等成为研究与政策中的固定复合术语。

items.en: Educational is recorded as the adjective of education; the dating is approximate.
items.cn: educational 作为 education 的形容词见于记载；此处年代为大致估计。

items.en: Education is borrowed from Latin educatio, naming the rearing and training of a child.
items.cn: education 借自拉丁语 educatio，指对儿童的养育与培养。

items.en: educare 'bring up, rear' and educere 'lead out' are related but not identical: educare is frequentative in form, suggesting repeated care, while educere stresses leading forth.
items.cn: educare“抚养、培育”与 educere“引出”相关但不相同：educare 形式上有反复意味，暗示持续的照料；educere 则强调“引出”。

items.en: ducere 'to lead' comes from PIE *deuk- 'to lead'. The same root gives duct, conduct, introduce and produce, all involving leading or bringing.
items.cn: ducere“引导”出自原始印欧语 *deuk-“引导”（重构形式）。同一词根给出 duct、conduct、introduce、produce，都含“引、带”之意。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives from two genuine different-root neighbours; the second compares words that share only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与两个不同词根的撞形词分开；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: a version of a published work. It comes from edere 'give out', from ex- plus dare 'give', not from educare 'rear'.
entries.definitionCN: 出版物的一种版本。它出自 edere“给出”，即 ex- 加 dare“给”，与 educare“养育”无关。

entries.definition: a large building. It comes from aedes 'building' plus facere 'make', with no connection to education.
entries.definitionCN: 大型建筑物。它出自 aedes“建筑”加 facere“制造”，与 education 无关。

entries.definition: the verb behind education, from educare. It is the source relation, not a look-alike.
entries.definitionCN: education 背后的动词，出自 educare。它是来源关系，不是撞形词。

entries.definition: giving useful information or a moral lesson. It is close to educational in sense 02, but stresses the lesson delivered.
entries.definitionCN: 提供有用信息或道德教训的。它与 educational 第 02 义接近，但强调所传递的教训。

entries.definition: relating to formal study at schools or universities. It is narrower than educational and often contrasts with practical.
entries.definitionCN: 与学校或大学的正式学习相关的。它比 educational 窄，且常与 practical 相对。

entries.definition: relating to teaching methods. It is more technical than educational and focuses on how, not what or where.
entries.definitionCN: 与教学方法相关的。它比 educational 更技术化，关注“怎么教”，而不是教什么、在哪里教。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: educational is education plus -al, the same pattern as national and personal.
normal.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al，和 national、personal 一样。

normal.en: The root educare 'rear' is related to educere 'lead out': teaching as leading someone out of where they were.
normal.cn: 词根 educare“养育”与 educere“引出”相关：教学就是把一个人从原处引出来。

normal.en: ducere 'lead' also gives conduct, introduce and produce.
normal.cn: ducere“引导”还给出 conduct、introduce、produce。

normal.en: edition and edifice look like education but belong to dare 'give' and facere 'make'.
normal.cn: edition 与 edifice 看着像 education，却分属 dare“给”与 facere“造”。

normal.en: A museum can be educational without being educational in the institutional sense.
normal.cn: 一座博物馆可以是 educational（有教益），却不必是制度意义上的 educational。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a blackboard extended past the lesson, and a student walking along it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上一条线被延长到课程之外，一名学生沿着它走。

abstract.en: The same line appears as a system, an attainment level, a toy, a technology, a psychology, an inequality, and a value.
abstract.cn: 同一条线可以显形为制度、受教育程度、玩具、技术、心理学、不平等与价值。

abstract.en: Every sense asks who is being led, and how far past the lesson they go.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在问：被引领的是谁，又比课程多走了多远。

examples.en: The museum runs educational programmes for local schools.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆为当地学校开设教育项目。

examples.en: The game is educational without feeling like homework.
examples.cn: 这个游戏有教育意义，却不像作业。

examples.en: Educational attainment varies widely across the region.
examples.cn: 该地区的受教育程度差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱就开心脑」——爱学习就开心动脑，越学越有教益 → educational 教育的、有教育意义的

root: 拉丁语 educatio“养育、培养”＝educare“抚养、培育”＋-atio（动作名词后缀）；educare 与 educere“引出”相关，后者＝ex-“出”＋ducere“引导”。educational＝education＋-al（形容词后缀）。核心是“把人从原处引出来”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a line drawn past the lesson. What changes is whether the line is an institution, an effect, a product, a level, a tool, a research field, a gap, or a value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一条画到课程之外的线。变化的只是这条线是制度、效果、产品、层级、工具、研究领域、差距，还是价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher extends a chalk line past what has been taught, and students follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把粉笔线延长到已教内容之外，学生顺着走。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND EFFECT: first the adjective marks what belongs to schooling, then what teaches outside it.
branches.cn: 制度与效果：形容词先标记属于学校教育的东西，再标记在校外教人的东西。

branches.en: MATERIALS: intent is built into toys and software, so the word describes design rather than result.
branches.cn: 材料：意图被做进玩具与软件，于是这个词描述设计而非结果。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the process is converted into years and certificates, a level that can be compared.
branches.cn: 测量：过程被换算成年数与证书，成为可比较的层级。

branches.en: A FIELD OF STUDY: one discipline applies itself to education, producing educational psychology.
branches.cn: 研究领域：一门学科把自身应用于教育，产生教育心理学。

branches.en: VALUE AND GAP: the same line lets policy locate inequality and lets critics ask what an object teaches.
branches.cn: 价值与差距：同一条线让政策定位不平等，也让批评者追问一物教了什么。

intro.en: Educational is education plus -al. The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, forms relational adjectives; English first borrowed education, then added the adjective ending.
intro.cn: educational 是 education 加 -al。后缀 -al 出自拉丁语 -alis，构成关系形容词；英语先借入 education，再加形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The base verb is educare 'bring up, rear', related to educere 'lead out' (ex- 'out' plus ducere 'lead'). ducere supplies duct-, visible in conduct, introduce and produce.
latinIntro.cn: 词基动词是 educare“抚养、培育”，与 educere“引出”（ex-“出”＋ducere“引导”）相关。ducere 提供 duct- 词干，见于 conduct、introduce、produce。

items.meaning: relating to education, or serving to teach
items.meaningCN: 与教育相关的；有教益的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The trip had real educational value.
items.exampleCN: 这次旅行有真正的教益。

items.meaning: the process of rearing and teaching
items.meaningCN: 养育与教学的过程（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.exampleCN: 教育在学校之前很久就开始了。

items.example: They educated their children at home.

items.meaningCN: 教育者（-or 表示施动者）
items.exampleCN: 这位教育者设计了课程。

items.example: The two districts are educationally unequal.
items.exampleCN: 这两个学区在教育上并不平等。

items.meaning: one who studies or promotes education
items.meaningCN: 教育学家；教育改革推动者
items.example: The educationalist argued for smaller classes.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育学家主张缩小班级规模。

items.meaning: having the power to teach or improve
items.meaningCN: 有教育作用的；能起教化作用的
items.example: The experience was educative rather than pleasant.
items.exampleCN: 这段经历与其说愉快，不如说有教益。

items.meaningCN: 可教育的；有学习能力的
items.example: The test measured whether the child was educable.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量这个孩子是否具备受教育能力。

items.meaningCN: 男女同校的（co- 表示“共同”）
items.exampleCN: 这所学院于 1970 年改为男女同校。

items.example: Good questions educe what students already suspect.
items.exampleCN: 好问题能引出学生已有的猜想。

latinEntries.meaning: a rearing, training; the source of education
latinEntries.meaningCN: 养育、培养；education 所本的拉丁动作名词

definition_zh: 努力；费力的一次尝试；费尽心力做出的成果；集体的协同行动；（物理学）作用力
definition_en: the physical or mental energy used when trying to do something
core_image: 一个人推着装满石头的木车，青筋鼓起，车轮在地面上压出一道痕
scene: 山路太陡，几个人一起推同一辆货车，车轮才勉强往前走。Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 指「为达成一件事而付出的体力或脑力」（第 1 个义项：付出力气去做）；句意为他们合力只把车推动了几米就不得不停下。图中可辨识物件：木车、陡坡、被压出的车辙、几双用力的腿。

pos.zh: 努力；尝试；费力得到的成果；协同行动

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「需要使力气的」
在形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「费力的」转为「以费力方式」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「看起来不费力气」
在否定式形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「不费力的」转为「毫不费力地」
在否定式形容词后加名词后缀构成，语义由「不费力」转为「不费力这一特质」

senses.title: Energy spent on a task
senses.titleCN: 为做成一件事付出的力气
senses.definition: the physical or mental energy that someone uses in trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人为做成某件事而投入的体力或脑力
senses.example: Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合力只把车推动了大约几米，就不得不停下休息。
senses.why: the word descends from a Latin verb meaning to strengthen, so the first sense is simply the strength that a task draws out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一个意为「使有力」的拉丁动词，所以第一个义项就是一件事从人身上抽出的那股力。

senses.title: A single attempt
senses.definition: one act of trying to do something, viewed as a countable attempt
senses.definitionCN: 试着做某事的一次行动，可以按次计数
senses.example: He made three efforts to lift the lid before asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着揭开盖子三次，才去求助。
senses.why: once energy is spent it can be counted as a try, so the noun shifts from the fuel to the event that burns it.
senses.whyCN: 力气一旦花出去，就可以说成「一次尝试」，于是名词从燃料转向烧掉燃料的那件事。

senses.title: A piece of work produced
senses.definition: a result or piece of work judged by how much care and labour went into it
senses.definitionCN: 按投入的心血与劳动来评价的成果或作品
senses.example: Her essay was a serious effort, even if the argument faltered.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章是一份认真写就的成果，尽管论证有些摇晃。
senses.why: we praise a thing by naming the labour inside it, so the word can stand for the product rather than the process.
senses.whyCN: 人们通过点出其中所含的劳动来称赞一件东西，于是这个词可以用产物代替过程。

senses.title: Organized collective action
senses.definition: a coordinated campaign in which many people work toward one public aim
senses.definitionCN: 许多人朝同一个公共目标协作推进的行动
senses.example: The relief effort reached the valley two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援行动抵达了山谷。
senses.why: when many people spend energy on one aim, the countable noun becomes the whole campaign rather than any single exertion.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人把力气投向一个目标时，这个可数名词指的就是整场行动，而不是任何单次用力。

senses.title: Force applied in a machine
senses.definition: in mechanics, the force applied to a machine or load, as opposed to the resistance it moves
senses.definitionCN: 力学中施加于机械或负载的力，与它所推动的阻力相对
senses.example: A longer lever increases the effect of the effort on the load.
senses.exampleCN: 较长的杠杆会增大作用力对负载的效果。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the plain meaning exactly: the force a worker puts in, measured against what the machine must move.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义保留了最朴素的意思：人使出的那股力，与机器要移动的东西相对而量。

senses.title: Degree of strain involved
senses.definition: the amount of strain a task demands, considered as a property of the task
senses.definitionCN: 任务所要求的紧张程度，作为任务本身的属性来看
senses.example: The climb costs little effort if you start early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果早点出发，这段爬坡并不费多少力气。
senses.why: instead of the energy itself, the word can name the quantity of it that a job requires, which is why one asks how much effort a task takes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指力气本身，而指一件事所需的力气分量，所以人们会问一项任务要花多少努力。

senses.title: National mobilization
senses.definition: the total organized activity of a country or a large body in wartime or emergency
senses.definitionCN: 战时或紧急状态下，一国或一个大型机构投入的全部组织性活动
senses.example: The war effort drew factories, farms and railways into one plan.
senses.exampleCN: 战时动员把工厂、农场与铁路都纳入一个计划。
senses.why: this is the collective sense enlarged to the scale of a whole society, where every exertion feeds a single campaign.
senses.whyCN: 这是集体义被放大到整个社会的规模：每一份力气都汇入同一场行动。

senses.title: An attempt judged kindly
senses.titleCN: 值得称许的一次尝试（即使未成）
senses.definition: an attempt that is praised for the honesty of the trying even though it falls short
senses.definitionCN: 即便未达到目标，也因尝试本身认真而受到赞许的一次努力
senses.example: The team lost, but it was a brave effort by every player.
senses.exampleCN: 球队输了，但每位队员的这次努力都很勇敢。
senses.why: because effort measures what was given rather than what was gained, the word becomes a way of honouring a failure.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词量的是付出而非所得，它就成了给失败留体面的一种说法。

intro.en: Effort comes through Old French esforz from the verb esforcier 'to force, exert', which rests on a Vulgar Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare, from Latin fortis 'strong'. The deeper origin of fortis is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 esforz 来自动词 esforcier「用力、使力」，后者基于一个被重构为 exfortiare 的俗拉丁动词，其词根为拉丁 fortis「强壮」。fortis 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, mighty, firm'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link proposed to a root for 'height' or 'mountain' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮、有力、坚固」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「高度」或「山」的词根相联系的看法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: A spoken-Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare 'to put forth strength' carried the root into the everyday speech of the late empire; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 一个被重构为 exfortiare 的口语拉丁动词「使出力气」，把词根带入帝国晚期日常口语；这一形式属重构，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French esforcier 'to force, strive, exert oneself' produced the noun esforz, which named both the strain and the try.
items.cn: 古法语 esforcier「用力、奋力、施展」产生名词 esforz，兼指那份紧张与那次尝试。

items.en: Middle English took the noun as effort in the fourteenth century, still close to the sense of a strong exertion of the will.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪把这个名词吸收为 effort，仍贴近「意志强力施展」的意思。

items.en: From the nineteenth century mechanics used effort for the applied force in a simple machine, set against the load it moves.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，力学用这个词指简单机械中施加的力，与被移动的负载相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of fortis and the exact spoken form): any Indo-European form offered for fortis is a reconstruction, and the earliest noun use has no securely dated citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（fortis 的更深来源与那个口语形式的确切面貌）：凡为 fortis 给出的印欧语形式均为重构形式；这个名词最早用法也没有确切年代的出处。

note.en: Group one collects words that look like effort but come from other roots; group two collects near neighbours that measure exertion differently.
note.cn: 第一组是形近而异源的词；第二组是语义相近、但衡量「付出」方式不同的词。

entries.definition: Its negation: work done without visible strain, so the strain is precisely what has vanished.
entries.definitionCN: 该词的否定形式：不显费力的工作，消失的正是那份紧张。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus fortis: what strengthens someone, hence ease and consolation, not exertion.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 fortis 构成：使人强健之物，因此指舒适与安慰，而非付出。

entries.definition: Fortis 'strong' plus facere 'to make': to make strong, as a wall or a body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 fortis「强壮」加 facere「做」构成：使变强，如城墙或身体。

entries.definition: Strength of mind under pain or pressure; it names the capacity rather than its spending.
entries.definitionCN: 痛苦或压力下心志的坚强；指那份能力，而不是它的耗费。

entries.definition: From for- 'outside' plus a Germanic root for a fine: to lose something as a penalty, with no link to strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 for-「在外」加一个表示罚金的日耳曼词根构成：作为惩罚而失去某物，与「强壮」无关。

entries.definition: The activity of labouring, named by what is done rather than by the strain it costs.
entries.definitionCN: 指劳动这项活动，以「做了什么」命名，而不以耗费多少力气命名。

entries.definition: A formal word for strong physical or mental strain; effort is its everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示强烈体力或脑力紧张的正式词；effort 是它日常的对应说法。

entries.definition: A try at something, with the outcome unknown; it says nothing about how much energy was spent.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的尝试，结果未知；不含花费了多少力气之意。

entries.definition: A sustained, purposeful effort, often on something public or grand; it carries a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 持久的、有目的的付出，多用于公共或宏大的事；语气正式。

entries.definition: Hard physical work, especially of a manual or repetitive kind; it stresses the grind.
entries.definitionCN: 艰苦的体力劳动，尤指手工或重复性工作；强调辛苦本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin fortis 'strong', so effort is strength brought out and spent.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此这个词就是被使出来、被花掉的力气。

normal.en: The family runs effort, effortless, effortful, effortlessly, effortlessness.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、肯定与否定两个形容词、副词与抽象名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spending: make an effort, put effort into, spare no effort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这份耗费：作出努力、投入心力、不遗余力。

normal.en: The technical use appears in the lever: effort acts on one arm, the load on the other.
normal.cn: 技术义出现在杠杆里：施力作用于一端，负载作用于另一端。

normal.en: Relatives outside the word still carry the same root: fortify, fortitude, comfort.
normal.cn: 词外的同族词仍然带着同一词根：加固、坚毅、安慰。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing water out of a cloth until the drops stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把布里的水拧出来，直到不再滴。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled taut between two posts, humming with the strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子在两根柱子之间被拉紧，绷得发出声。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burned down to a stub because it was kept lit all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛因为整夜点着，只剩下一小截。

examples.en: It took a full day of effort to clear the blocked channel.
examples.cn: 清理这条堵塞的水道花了整整一天的力气。

examples.en: The rescue effort involved boats, dogs and six villages.
examples.cn: 这次救援行动动用了船只、犬只与六个村庄的人手。

examples.en: A lever lets a small effort lift a heavy load.
examples.cn: 杠杆使小小的作用力能抬起沉重的负载。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一夫」推车——一个人使出全身力气推车 → 努力、费力

root: 古法语 esforz「力气、奋力」→ 俗拉丁重构形式 exfortiare「使出力气」→ 拉丁 fortis「强壮、有力」；fortis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: strength is drawn out of a body, counted as a try, then read into the thing made, into the group that shares it, into the machine that measures it, into the size of the demand, into a whole nation's campaign and finally into the praise given to a losing attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：力气从身体里被抽出，先被数成一次尝试，再被读进做出的东西、共担的群体、量它的机械、需求的大小、举国的动员，最后读进给失败尝试的那份称许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body braced against a loaded cart, strength visibly leaving it and entering the work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体抵着装满货物的车，力气看得见地从身体里流出，进入那件活里。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY AND ITS SIZE: energy itself, and the amount of it a task calls for.
branches.cn: 储备与其分量：力气本身，以及一件事要调用多少。

branches.en: THE COUNTED TRY: one attempt, and the same attempt judged generous even when it fails.
branches.cn: 被数出的尝试：一次尝试，以及这次尝试即便落空也被评得宽厚。

branches.en: THE THING MADE: labour can be read back out of the result.
branches.cn: 做出的东西：劳动可以从成果里被读回来。

branches.en: THE SHARED CAMPAIGN: many bodies push one aim, from a rescue to a whole nation.
branches.cn: 共担的行动：许多身体推同一个目标，从一次救援到一个国家。

branches.en: THE MEASURED FORCE: mechanics turns the body's push into a quantity on one arm of a lever.
branches.cn: 被量住的力：力学把身体的推力化成一个落在杠杆一端的量。

intro.en: Effort is a noun taken whole from Old French, so it has no live prefixes for English speakers; what grows from it are suffixes and a root that still builds other words.
intro.cn: 这个词是从古法语整体借入的名词，对英语使用者来说没有可拆的活前缀；从它长出来的是后缀，以及一个仍在构成别的词的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis 'strong' also gives fortify, fortitude and comfort; the suffix -less and -ful build the two opposite adjectives from the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」还衍生出 fortify、fortitude 与 comfort；后缀 -less 与 -ful 从名词造出两个相反的形容词。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「力量」的意思。

items.structure: Old French esforz, noun of esforcier
items.example: The effort cost them a whole day.
items.exampleCN: 这份努力花了他们一整天。

items.example: An effortful climb ended at the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 一段费力的攀登在岭上结束。

items.example: She breathed effortfully on the last stretch.
items.exampleCN: 最后一段她呼吸得很费力。
他的划水看起来毫不费力。
滑翔机毫不费力地升了上去。

items.example: The effortlessness was the result of years of drill.
items.exampleCN: 这种毫不费力是多年苦练的结果。

items.example: They fortified the bank against the current.
items.exampleCN: 他们加固了堤岸以抗水流。

items.example: She met the loss with fortitude.
items.exampleCN: 她以坚毅面对这次损失。

items.example: The blanket gave the child comfort.
items.exampleCN: 这条毯子给了孩子安慰。

latinEntries.structure: exfortiare (reconstructed Vulgar Latin verb, first conjugation)

definition_en: an oval object with a hard shell laid by a bird, containing a young bird or the female reproductive cell of an animal
core_image: 蛋壳里包着的小生命：一层硬壳护住未来的生命
scene: 早餐的平底锅里，一个白白的圆东西正在滋滋作响。She fried an egg and put it on top of the rice.
sceneCN: 这里 egg 是「鸡蛋」（第 1 个义项：禽类的卵）；句意是她煎了一个鸡蛋放在米饭上。图中可辨识物件：平底锅、滋滋作响的煎蛋、米饭、热气。

senses.title: A bird egg that people eat
senses.definition: an oval object with a shell, laid by a hen or other bird, that people cook and eat
senses.definitionCN: 母鸡或其他禽类产下的带壳椭圆物，人们把它煮着吃或煎着吃。
senses.example: I boiled two eggs for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 我早餐煮了两个鸡蛋。
senses.why: The core image is a small life sealed in a shell, and cooking turns that sealed life into food.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是壳里封着的小生命，而烹饪把这个被封存的生命变成了食物。

senses.title: The female reproductive cell
senses.definition: the female cell of an animal or plant that can join with a male cell to produce a new life
senses.definitionCN: 动物或植物的雌性生殖细胞，能与雄性细胞结合产生新生命。
senses.example: A human egg is far larger than a sperm.
senses.exampleCN: 人类的卵细胞比精子大得多。
senses.why: Because every egg holds the seed of new life, biology extends the word from a hen's egg to the smallest female cell.
senses.whyCN: 因为每个蛋都孕育着新生命，生物学便把这个词从鸡蛋延伸到最小的雌性细胞。

senses.title: An egg-shaped thing
senses.definition: something shaped like an egg
senses.definitionCN: 形状像蛋一样的东西。
senses.example: She cut the soap into a smooth egg.
senses.exampleCN: 她把肥皂削成一个光滑的蛋形。
senses.why: Anything oval with one end slightly bigger reminds us of the shape of an egg.
senses.whyCN: 凡是椭圆、一端略大的形状，都会让人想起蛋的外形。

senses.title: To throw eggs at someone
senses.definition: to throw eggs at a person or building as an attack
senses.definitionCN: 把蛋扔向某人或某建筑物以示攻击。
senses.example: Fans egged the singer's car after the show.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束后，歌迷向歌手的车扔鸡蛋。
senses.why: A rotten egg makes a mess, so throwing one becomes a cheap way to insult someone.
senses.whyCN: 臭蛋砸开一片狼藉，于是扔蛋成了羞辱人的廉价方式。

intro.en: Egg is one of the oldest everyday words in English, and its history includes a famous medieval misunderstanding.
intro.cn: egg 是英语里最古老的日常词之一，它的历史里还藏着一段著名的中世纪误会。

items.en: Old Norse egg, the same root that gave Scandinavian languages their word for egg, was brought to England by Viking settlers.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 egg，即斯堪的纳维亚语言中表示蛋的词，由维京定居者带到英格兰。

items.en: Native Old English used a different word, oeg, which was already fading when the Norse form arrived.
items.cn: 本土古英语原本用的是另一个词 oeg，在诺斯形式到来时已经衰落。

items.en: A famous anecdote from 1448 claims the grammarian Caxton confused Northern egg with Southern eyren, showing both forms lived side by side.
items.cn: 1448 年的著名轶事说语法学家卡克斯顿分不清北方的 egg 与南方的 eyren，可见两种形式并存过。

items.en: The Norse form gradually won out and egg spread across England in both literal and figurative uses.
items.cn: 诺斯形式逐渐胜出，egg 以本义和引申义传遍英格兰。

items.en: Modern English keeps egg as the everyday word and has coined phrases like egg on and a good egg.
items.cn: 现代英语中 egg 仍是日常词，并衍生出 egg on、a good egg 等短语。

note.en: Words that resemble egg either share its sound or live in the same kitchen-and-birth word field.
note.cn: 下面两组词要么与 egg 音形相近，要么同处厨房与生育的语义场。

entries.definitionCN: 自我；自负——只是拼读与 egg 相近，词义无关

entries.definition: the line where a surface ends
entries.definitionCN: 边缘；棱——发音与 egg 相近，词源不同
乞求——拼写与 egg 相近，词义完全不同
椭圆形的；蛋形的

entries.definition: the hard outer covering of an egg
entries.definitionCN: 壳；蛋壳——egg 的组成部分

entries.definition: the yellow middle part of an egg
entries.definitionCN: 蛋黄——egg 的内部结构

normalIntro.en: Five hooks that tie egg to its shell, its life, and its phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五条联想，把 egg 与壳、生命和常用短语绑在一起。

normal.en: The word egg sounds like a single short knock on a shell.
normal.cn: egg 读起来像在蛋壳上轻轻敲一下。

normal.en: A hen sits on an egg to guard a new life.
normal.cn: 母鸡伏在蛋上守护新生命。

normal.en: Lay an egg literally means produce an egg, but idiomatically means to fail badly.
normal.cn: lay an egg 字面是下蛋，引申为彻底失败。

normal.en: Egg someone on means push them forward like nudging a shell.
normal.cn: egg someone on 意为怂恿，像推一把壳往前滚。

normal.en: A good egg is a reliable person, just like a fresh egg you can trust.
normal.cn: a good egg 指可靠的人，就像一枚让人放心的新鲜蛋。

abstract.en: Picture every morning starting with a small round sun in a pan.
abstract.cn: 想象每个清晨从锅里一枚圆圆的小太阳开始。

abstract.en: See a hard shell hiding a soft, waiting life inside.
abstract.cn: 看见硬壳里藏着柔软而等待绽放的生命。

abstract.en: Feel the crack when a shell breaks and a new day begins.
abstract.cn: 感受蛋壳裂开时新一天开始的那声脆响。

examples.en: She fried an egg and put it on top of the rice.
examples.cn: 她煎了一个鸡蛋放在米饭上。

examples.en: A human egg is far larger than a sperm.
examples.cn: 人类的卵细胞比精子大得多。

examples.en: Don't egg him on; he is angry enough already.
examples.cn: 别再怂恿他了，他已经够生气了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哎咯」——母鸡下完蛋总会「哎咯哎咯」地叫，一叫就想到 egg。

root: egg 来自古诺斯语 egg，与本族古英语 oeg 并存后胜出；日耳曼语族同源词遍布北欧语言。

sensesIntro.en: From breakfast food to the smallest unit of life, egg spreads over concrete and scientific senses.
sensesIntro.cn: egg 从早餐食物延伸到最小的生命单元，覆盖具体与科学两类义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small life sealed in a hard shell
core.cn: 核心意象：硬壳里封存的小生命

branches.en: from hen's egg to living cell

intro.en: Egg itself carries no prefix or suffix, so this map collects its family and common egg-related words.
intro.cn: egg 本身无前缀后缀，这里整理其词族与常见的 egg 相关词。

latinIntro.en: Egg is Germanic, so Latin-rooted relatives are limited to food-science terms.
latinIntro.cn: egg 属日耳曼词源，拉丁词族仅见于食品科学术语。

items.meaning: the hard outer layer of an egg
items.example: The bird rose from a broken eggshell.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟从破碎的蛋壳中站起。

items.meaning: the yellow part inside an egg
items.example: Separate the eggyolk from the white.

items.meaning: having the taste or smell of egg
items.example: The kitchen smelled eggy after breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 早餐后厨房里满是蛋味。

items.meaning: a purple vegetable named for its egg-like shape
items.meaningCN: 茄子——因果实形似蛋得名

items.example: The lab is full of eggheads.

items.meaning: a creamy drink made with eggs

items.example: She built a nest egg for retirement.
items.exampleCN: 她为退休攒下了储备金。

items.meaning: something with both good and bad parts
items.example: The plan is a curate's egg.

items.meaning: to urge someone to do something risky
items.example: His friends egged him on to dive.
The team scored a goose egg.

definition_en: the number equal to seven plus one
core_image: 两摞叠起的方块：上下各四个，凑成八
scene: 教室墙上的挂钟刚敲响，指针停在固定的位置。The class begins at eight every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 eight 是「八点」（第 1 个义项：数字八）；句意是课每天早上八点开始。图中可辨识物件：挂钟、指针、教室墙壁、书包。

senses.title: The number 8
senses.definition: the number equal to seven plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于七加一的数字。
senses.example: The class begins at eight every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 课每天早上八点开始。
senses.why: Counting from a full hand of five plus three more fingers gives the concrete image of eight.
senses.whyCN: 从一只手的五根手指再加三根，就得到八的具体形象。

senses.title: A group of eight people or things
senses.definition: a set of eight players, rowers, or items
senses.definitionCN: 由八人（如赛艇）或八物组成的一组。
senses.example: The boat crew rowed as a strong eight.
senses.exampleCN: 这支赛艇队作为八人组划得很有力。
senses.why: A number can stand for the team that fills it, so eight becomes the crew itself.
senses.whyCN: 数字可以代指以它编成的队伍，于是 eight 就成了那支八人队。

senses.title: The age of eight
senses.definition: the age of being eight years old
senses.definitionCN: 八岁的年龄。
senses.example: My daughter started piano at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 我女儿八岁开始学琴。
senses.why: Ages are said with bare numbers, so eight alone can mean the age.
senses.whyCN: 年龄用裸数字表达，于是 eight 单独就能指八岁。

intro.en: Eight goes straight back to an ancient counting word shared across Germanic and even further.
intro.cn: eight 直接回溯到一个跨日耳曼乃至更早的古代计数词。

items.en: Proto-Germanic ahto, the shared ancestor of all Germanic number words for eight.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 ahto，是各日耳曼语言八字的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English eahta or ahta, written in the earliest surviving texts.
items.cn: 古英语 eahta 或 ahta，见于现存最早的文献。

items.en: Middle English eighte regularized the ending under the influence of ten and fifteen.
items.cn: 中古英语 eighte 在 ten、fifteen 类比下规整了词尾。

items.en: Modern English shortened the vowel and fixed the spelling eight, where gh is silent.
items.cn: 现代英语缩短元音，定型拼法 eight，其中 gh 不发音。

items.en: Compounds like eighteen, eighty and eighth were then formed by regular pattern.
items.cn: 此后按规则模式派生出 eighteen、eighty、eighth 等合成词。

note.en: Two groups: words that look or sound like eight, and words from the same number family.

senses.title: The number 18
senses.definition: the number equal to ten plus eight
senses.definitionCN: 等于十加八的数字。
senses.example: She turned eighteen last Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 她上周六满十八岁。

senses.title: The age of adulthood

senses.example: You can vote once you are eighteen.

items.en: Old English said ahtatene, putting the unit eight before the ten, like modern German achtzehn.
items.cn: 古英语 ahtatene，个位八在前、十在后，语序如现代德语 achtzehn。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic pattern units-plus-teen governed all teen numbers.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼「个位加十」的模式统辖所有 -teen 数词。

items.en: Middle English eighteen settled into the fixed form still used today.
items.cn: 中古英语定型为 eighteen，沿用至今。

items.en: Modern English treats eighteen as one word with its own stress on -teen.
items.cn: 现代英语把 eighteen 视为一个词，重音落在 -teen。

items.en: Its ordinal eighteenth and the related eighty grew by regular suffixes.
items.cn: 序数 eighteenth 与相关词 eighty 按规则后缀派生。

note.en: Compare eighteen with its look-alikes and the numbers that surround it.

senses.title: Position 18 in a series

senses.definitionCN: 排在十七个之后的位置或顺序。
senses.example: He lives on the eighteenth floor.

senses.why: Adding the ordinal ending -th turns the counting word into a position word.
senses.whyCN: 加上序数词尾 -th，就把计数词变成了位置词。

senses.title: The eighteenth century period

senses.title: Position 8 in a series

intro.cn: eighty 体现了日耳曼语用个位构整十的老习惯。

items.en: Old English hundeahtatig, literally a hundred-eight-ten block, meant eighty.
items.cn: 古英语 hundeahtatig，字面为百-八-十的组合，意为八十。

items.en: Proto-Germanic built tens as units plus a ten suffix, ahtōtehund.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语以个位加十后缀构整十数，如 ahtōtehund。

items.en: Middle English eighti contracted the long Old English form into eighty.
items.cn: 中古英语 eighti 把冗长的古英语形式紧缩为 eighty。

items.en: Modern English fixed the -ty spelling that matches twenty and sixty.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 -ty 拼法，与 twenty、sixty 一致。

items.en: The decade sense of the eighties arose with modern calendar talk.
items.cn: the eighties 的年代义随现代纪年表达而产生。

note.en: Watch the spelling shift between eighty and its teens cousin; the meaning group collects decade words.
note.cn: 注意 eighty 与 teens 表亲的拼写差异；近义组收集年代词汇。

definition_zh: 任一；（否定）也；两者之一的
definition_en: one or the other of two; used after a negative to mean also not
core_image: 双手各托一样东西，让你挑任意一边
scene: 餐桌上摆着两只杯子，妈妈让孩子随便挑一杯。Take either cup, the milk is the same.
sceneCN: 这里 either 是「任意一个」（第 1 个义项：两者之一）；句意是随便拿哪只杯都行，奶是一样的。图中可辨识物件：餐桌、两只杯子、牛奶、孩子的手。

senses.title: One or the other of two
senses.definition: one or the other of two people or things
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或物之中的任意一个。
senses.example: Take either cup, the milk is the same.
senses.exampleCN: 随便拿哪只杯都行，奶是一样的。
senses.why: The old root meant one of two, so either keeps the image of two choices side by side.
senses.whyCN: 古词根本义即「两者之一」，either 保留了两个选项并排的画面。

senses.title: Also not, after a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to add another negative
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句后补充同样的否定。
senses.example: I do not like it either.
senses.exampleCN: 我也不喜欢它。
senses.why: The parallel sense grew out of listing two items, one of which is also excluded.
senses.whyCN: 并列义源于列举两项而其中一项同样被排除。

senses.title: Correlating two alternatives
senses.definition: used with or to present two alternatives
senses.definitionCN: 与 or 搭配提出两个可选方案。
senses.example: Either you apologize, or you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 要么道歉，要么离开。
senses.why: Pairing either with or builds a fork in the road, one branch to be chosen.
senses.whyCN: either 与 or 搭配搭出岔路口，两条分支必选其一。

intro.en: Either and its sister neither go back to one old word meaning each of two.
intro.cn: either 与它的姊妹词 neither 源自同一个表示「两者各一」的古词。

items.en: Old English oegther, from oegther, meaning each of two.
items.cn: 古英语 oegther，意为「两者各一」。

items.en: The root aiwaz or aiz, a Germanic word for a group of two, spread across the family.
items.cn: 词根 aiwaz 或 aiz，表示「一组两个」的日耳曼词，传遍语族。

items.en: Middle English either took its modern shape and began the either... or... pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语 either 形成现代形态并开启 either...or... 结构。

items.en: Modern English uses either for choices, and neither for double negation.
items.cn: 现代英语用 either 表选择，neither 表双重否定。

items.en: Pronunciation split into British and American variants over the centuries.
items.cn: 数百年间读音分化出不列颠与美利坚两种变体。

note.en: Either lives between choice words and negative twins.
note.cn: either 处于选择词与否定孪生词之间。

definition_en: the joint between the upper and lower arm; to push with the elbows
core_image: 手臂的弯头：像管道一样能折角的关节
scene: 拥挤的车厢里，有人轻轻用胳膊弯开路。He elbowed his way through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 elbow 是「用肘推挤」（第 2 个义项：用肘部推）；句意是他用肘挤过人群。图中可辨识物件：车厢、拥挤的人群、抬起的手臂、抓稳的扶手。

senses.title: The arm joint
senses.definition: the joint where the arm bends
senses.definitionCN: 手臂弯曲处的关节。
senses.example: He rested his elbows on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把肘部支在桌上。
senses.why: The bend of the arm looks like the bend of a pipe, which anchors the whole word family.
senses.whyCN: 手臂的弯折形似管道弯头，这为整个词族提供了锚点。

senses.title: To push with the elbow
senses.definition: to push people aside using your elbows
senses.definitionCN: 用肘部把人挤开以前进。
senses.example: He elbowed his way through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他用肘挤过人群。
senses.why: Because elbows are hard points, they become tools for forcing a path.
senses.whyCN: 肘是硬点，于是成了强行开路的工具。

senses.title: A bend shaped like an elbow
senses.definition: a pipe or fitting bent like an arm joint
senses.definitionCN: 形似手臂关节的弯管或接头。
senses.example: Plumbers fitted a copper elbow.
senses.exampleCN: 水管工安装了一个铜弯头。
senses.why: The bend of the arm transfers to any sharp-angled bend, especially in plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 手臂的弯折转移到任何锐角弯折处，尤见于管道。

items.en: Modern English keeps both noun and verb uses, plus idioms like elbow room.

definition_zh: 电；电力；电荷；电学；强烈的兴奋感
definition_en: the physical effect of electric charge, the power supplied through wires, or a tense feeling of excitement
core_image: 看不见的电流在铜线里奔跑，一按开关，整间屋子的灯同时亮起
scene: 雷雨夜里，整条街的灯忽然同时熄灭，只有远处的闪电把屋顶照白。When the storm cut the electricity, the whole street went dark at once.
sceneCN: 这里 electricity 指「送入住户与街道的电力供应」（第 4 个义项：供电、用电）；句意为暴风雨切断供电时，整条街同时黑了。图中可辨识物件：闪电、熄灭的路灯、窗户里的烛光、雨幕。

pos.zh: 兴奋的情绪张力；强烈的活力（不可数）

senses.title: The physical phenomenon
senses.titleCN: 电：电荷及其效应这一物理现象
senses.definition: the physical phenomenon of electric charge, its movement and its effects
senses.definitionCN: 电荷及其运动与效应构成的物理现象
senses.example: Electricity is easiest to see when it jumps across a gap as a spark.
senses.exampleCN: 电最容易看见的时候，是它作为火花跳过一道缝隙。
senses.why: The word names an invisible event that becomes visible only at its edge, which is why early students spoke of a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是看不见的事件，只在边缘才现形，因此早期研究者把它说成一种流体。

senses.title: Power sold as energy
senses.titleCN: 电能、电力：作为能源使用的电
senses.definition: electric power treated as a form of energy that can be generated and sold
senses.definitionCN: 把电当作可以生产、出售的一种能源
senses.example: The plant sells electricity to three neighbouring towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电厂向邻近的三个镇供电。
senses.why: Once electricity could be metered and billed, the phenomenon turned into a commodity measured in units.
senses.whyCN: 当电能被计量、收费，这个现象就变成了以单位计价的商品。

senses.title: Charge carried by particles
senses.definition: the electric charge that particles carry and transfer
senses.definitionCN: 粒子携带与转移的电荷
senses.example: Rubbing the rod transfers electricity to the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 摩擦棒子把电荷转移到布上。
senses.why: The word can point at the quantity itself rather than at the effect, especially when it moves from one body to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指向那个量本身，而不是效应，尤其当它从一个物体转到另一个物体时。

senses.title: The supply to a building
senses.titleCN: 供电、用电：送到房屋或街道的电
senses.definition: the supply of electric power to a building, a street or a region
senses.definitionCN: 向房屋、街道或地区输送的电力
senses.example: When the storm cut the electricity, the whole street went dark at once.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断供电时，整条街同时黑了。
senses.why: In daily speech people say the electricity for the service they buy, not for the physics behind it.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语里，人们用这个词指自己买到的服务，而不是背后的物理原理。

senses.title: Charge that stays put
senses.titleCN: 静电：停留在物体上的电荷
senses.definition: charge that gathers on an object and stays there until it is discharged
senses.definitionCN: 聚集在物体上、直到被释放才消失的电荷
senses.example: Walking across the carpet built up enough electricity to make a spark.
senses.exampleCN: 走过地毯积起的静电足以打出一个火花。
senses.why: A stored charge has no circuit to flow through, so it sits still and surprises the hand that touches it.
senses.whyCN: 被储存的电荷没有回路可走，于是停在原处，吓到伸手去碰的人。

senses.title: The branch of physics
senses.titleCN: 电学：研究电荷的物理分支
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies electric charge, current and related effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究电荷、电流及相关效应的物理分支
senses.example: He studied electricity before switching to acoustics.
senses.exampleCN: 他先学电学，后来转去研究声学。
senses.why: A phenomenon with laws and instruments turns into a subject taught under its own name.
senses.whyCN: 一个有定律、有仪器的现象，会变成以自己名字授课的学科。

senses.title: Tension in a room
senses.titleCN: 情绪张力：现场紧张而兴奋的气氛
senses.definition: a tense, exciting feeling that seems to fill a room or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 似乎充满房间或表演现场的紧张兴奋感
senses.example: The electricity in the hall rose as the band took the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队登台时，礼堂里的紧张感一下子升高了。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the spark: something invisible passes between people and makes the air feel charged.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了火花：某种看不见的东西在人与人之间传递，让空气像带了电。

senses.title: Energy in a place
senses.titleCN: 抽象活力：让地方振作起来的劲头
senses.definition: a feeling of energy and excitement that spreads through a place or a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方或群体中扩散开来的活力与兴奋
senses.example: The new plan brought electricity to a tired neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 新方案给一个疲惫的社区带来了生气。
senses.why: The abstract sense widens the charge from a room to a whole district, where the current is social rather than electrical.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把电荷从一间屋子扩展到整个街区，那里的电流是社会的，而不是电学的。

intro.en: Electricity was coined in the seventeenth century on the Greek word for amber, the substance that first showed the effect. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: electricity 于十七世纪用希腊语中「琥珀」一词造出，琥珀正是最早显现这一效应的物质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek ēlektron meant amber, and rubbed amber was known to attract light objects such as straw and feathers. The deeper origin of the Greek word is source uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 ēlektron 意为琥珀，人们早已知道摩擦过的琥珀能吸引草屑、羽毛等轻物。这个希腊词更深层的来源属于来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as electrum, which named both amber and a pale gold alloy; English took the same stem through learned Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊名词作 electrum，既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金；英语经学术拉丁语继承了同一词干。

items.en: William Gilbert coined electricus around 1600 for substances that behave like rubbed amber, using the Latin stem rather than the Greek one.
items.cn: 吉尔伯特约在 1600 年造出 electricus，指行为像摩擦琥珀的物质，用的是拉丁词干而非希腊词干。

items.en: English electric appears in the seventeenth century as the adjective for that attracting power, and electricity follows as its noun.
items.cn: 英语 electric 在十七世纪出现，用作这种吸引力的形容词，随后 electricity 作为名词跟上。

items.en: Sir Thomas Browne is often credited with the first English use of electricity in the 1640s; the exact date is approximate and the spelling varied.
items.cn: 人们常把 electricity 最早的英语使用归给托马斯·布朗，时在十七世纪四十年代；确切年代只是约数，拼写也多有变化。

items.en: Nineteenth-century generators turned electricity into a public supply, and twentieth-century writing extended the word to the excitement felt in a crowd.
items.cn: 十九世纪的发电机把电变成公共供应，二十世纪的写作又把这个词扩展到人群中的兴奋感。

note.en: Group one holds relatives and look-alikes of the electric stem; group two holds the physical quantities people mix it up with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 electric 词干的亲属词与形近词；第二组是常被与它混淆的物理量。

entries.definition: Describes a device or effect that works by electricity; electricity is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容靠电工作的装置或效应；electricity 是对应名词。

entries.definition: The broader adjective for systems and engineering, not for a single working device.
entries.definitionCN: 更广的形容词，用于系统与工程，而非单台工作装置。

entries.definition: The negatively charged particle; electricity is the flow or effect of such particles.
entries.definitionCN: 带负电的粒子；electricity 是这些粒子的流动或效应。

entries.definition: A person who installs and repairs wiring; the ending -ian marks a trade.
entries.definitionCN: 安装与维修线路的人；-ian 后缀标记职业。

entries.definition: The general word for energy delivered to homes, measured in watts; electricity is one form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指送到住户的能量，以瓦计量；electricity 是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: The rate at which charge moves through a wire; it is the flow, not the supply.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷在导线中移动的速率；指流动，而非供应。

entries.definition: The amount of electricity a body carries, measured in coulombs.
entries.definitionCN: 物体所带电的量，以库仑计量。

entries.definition: The capacity to do work in any form; electricity is only one carrier of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的做功能力；电只是它的一种载体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek source, the real derivatives and the real phrases of the electricity family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊语来源、真实的派生词，以及电这个词族里真实的搭配。

normal.en: The word began with amber: rubbed amber pulled straw, and the effect was named after the stuff.
normal.cn: 这个词从琥珀开始：摩擦过的琥珀能吸草屑，效应就以这种材料命名。

normal.en: The family runs electric, electrical, electrician, electrify, electrification and electronics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 electric、electrical、electrician、electrify、electrification 与 electronics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the supply sense: generate electricity, electricity supply, electricity bill.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出供应义：发电、电力供应、电费账单。

normal.en: The adjective and the noun split the work: electric device, electrical system, electricity supply.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词分工：电动的装置、电气的系统、电力的供应。

normal.en: Static electricity is charge with nowhere to go, which is why it waits and then shocks.
normal.cn: 静电是无处可去的电荷，因此它先等在那里，然后电你一下。

abstract.en: Picture water in a pipe: the pressure is voltage, the flow is current, and the water itself is charge.
abstract.cn: 想象水管里的水：水压是电压，水流是电流，水本身是电荷。

abstract.en: Picture a spark as the moment the invisible becomes visible.
abstract.cn: 想象火花就是看不见的东西现形的那一瞬。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone speaks at once and the air itself seems to hum.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人同时开口，连空气都像在嗡嗡作响。

examples.en: The village lived without electricity for a week after the line came down.
examples.cn: 线路倒下之后，村子过了一周没有电的日子。

examples.en: Copper wire carries electricity better than iron does.
examples.cn: 铜线导电比铁好。

examples.en: There was electricity in the room when the two rivals finally met.
examples.cn: 两个对手终于见面时，屋里充满了紧张的气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: electr-（琥珀）+ -icity（性质、状态）——摩擦琥珀吸起草屑的那种性质 → 电；供电

root: 希腊 ēlektron（琥珀）→ 拉丁 electrum → 新拉丁 electricus（吉尔伯特，约 1600）→ 英语 electric → electricity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from an invisible physical event to a commodity, a quantity, a household service, a stored charge, a science, and finally to the excitement in a room and in a district.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从看不见的物理事件走到商品、数量、住户服务、储存的电荷、一门学科，最后落到房间与街区里的兴奋感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible current running through copper, switching a whole building into light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的电流在铜线里奔跑，把整栋楼点亮。

branches.en: The phenomenon and the quantity: what happens, and how much of it a body carries.
branches.cn: 现象与数量：发生了什么，以及物体带了多少。

branches.en: The commodity and the household service it becomes once it is metered.
branches.cn: 商品与住户服务：一旦被计量，它就变成这两样东西。

branches.en: Charge that cannot move, waiting on a surface to surprise the next hand.
branches.cn: 不能移动的电荷，停在表面等着吓到下一只手。

branches.en: The effects made into a subject with laws, instruments and textbooks.
branches.cn: 把种种效应变成一门有定律、仪器与教科书的学科。

branches.en: The spark detached from wires and felt as tension in a room or energy in a district.
branches.cn: 火花脱离导线，被感受为屋里的紧张或街区的生气。

intro.en: Electricity is a noun on the electric stem with -ity, and the whole family reads from the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 词干加 -ity 构成的名词，整个词族都可以从希腊语「琥珀」读起。

latinIntro.en: Greek ēlektron gave Latin electrum, and New Latin electricus supplied the stem on which English built every derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 ēlektron 给出拉丁 electrum，新拉丁 electricus 提供词干，英语在其上构造了全部派生词。

core_image: 灰色巨兽甩着长鼻子走过草原
scene: 动物园里孩子们踮着脚看栅栏后的庞然大物。The baby elephant splashed water with its trunk.

senses.title: The animal
senses.definition: a huge grey mammal with a trunk and tusks
senses.definitionCN: 长有长鼻与象牙的巨大灰色哺乳动物。
senses.example: The baby elephant splashed water with its trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 小象用鼻子溅起水花。
senses.why: The trunk and grey hide form the fixed image that every sense grows from.
senses.whyCN: 长鼻与灰色厚皮构成固定意象，所有义项都由此生长。

senses.title: Something enormous and cumbersome
senses.definition: a very large, heavy, or clumsy thing
senses.definitionCN: 巨大、沉重或笨拙的东西。
senses.example: The old printing press was an elephant in the workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧印刷机在车间里像头巨兽。
senses.why: Size alone transfers the name of the biggest land animal to anything oversized.
senses.whyCN: 单凭体型，陆地最大动物的名字就转指任何超大的东西。

senses.title: A costly useless possession
senses.definition: an expensive possession that is hard to keep and useless
senses.definitionCN: 维护成本高而无实际用途的财产。
senses.example: The new stadium became a white elephant.
senses.exampleCN: 新体育场成了白象般的累赘。
senses.why: A legendary king supposedly gave white elephants as ruinous gifts, so the phrase stuck.
senses.whyCN: 传说某国王把白象作为令受赠者破产的礼物，短语因此流传。

intro.en: Elephant traveled through Greek and Latin before settling in English.
intro.cn: elephant 经希腊语、拉丁语辗转才在英语中安家。

items.en: Greek elephas first meant ivory, then the animal itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 elephas 最初指象牙，后转指动物本身。

items.en: Latin elephantus borrowed the Greek word with both meanings.
items.cn: 拉丁语 elephantus 连义借入该希腊词。

items.en: Old French olifant carried the word into medieval Europe, also naming a horn.
items.cn: 古法语 olifant 把词传入中世纪欧洲，也用来称一种号角。

items.en: Middle English elefaun and olifaunt alternate before the Greek-shaped spelling wins.
items.cn: 中古英语 elefaun 与 olifaunt 并存，最终希腊式拼法胜出。

items.en: Modern English standardizes elephant and coins idioms like white elephant.
items.cn: 现代英语定型 elephant 并衍生 white elephant 等习语。

definition_en: the number equal to ten plus one
core_image: 十根手指之外竖起的第一根手指
scene: 篮球队里刚好凑齐一队人马在训练。She scored eleven points in one game.
sceneCN: 这里 eleven 是「十一个」（第 1 个义项：数字十一）；句意是她在一场比赛得了十一分。图中可辨识物件：球场、记分牌、投篮的女孩、队友。

senses.title: The number 11
senses.definition: the number equal to ten plus one
senses.definitionCN: 等于十加一的数字。
senses.example: She scored eleven points in one game.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一场比赛得了十一分。
senses.why: The old root means one left over, the first digit standing beyond ten.
senses.whyCN: 古词根本义即「剩一」，是超过十之后竖起的第一根手指。

senses.title: An eleven-member team
senses.definition: a soccer or cricket team of eleven players
senses.definitionCN: 足球或板球的十一人队伍。
senses.example: The local eleven won the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 本地十一人队捧杯。
senses.why: The number stands for the whole squad that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 数字代指以它编成的整支队伍。

senses.title: The age of eleven
senses.definition: the age of being eleven years old

senses.example: He learned to swim at eleven.
senses.exampleCN: 他十一岁学会游泳。
senses.why: Ages are said with bare numbers, so eleven alone names the age.
senses.whyCN: 年龄用裸数字表达，eleven 单独即指该年龄。

intro.en: Eleven hides an old phrase meaning one left over after ten.

items.en: Old English endleofan, built on eofe or endleofan, meaning one left over ten.

items.en: Proto-Germanic ainalif, literally one-lief, one left beyond ten.

items.en: Middle English endlevente shortened to eleven through heavy slurring.
items.cn: 中古英语经重读弱化缩为 eleven。

items.en: Modern English spells it eleven with a single l and a soft v.

definition_en: coming after ten others in order, or one part of eleven equal parts
core_image: 时钟两针重合指向十一点的那一格
scene: 比赛还剩最后一分钟，替补队员在场边热身。The rescue came at the eleventh hour.

senses.definition: coming after ten others in order
senses.definitionCN: 排在十个之后的位置。
senses.example: The rescue came at the eleventh hour.
senses.exampleCN: 救援在最后关头赶到。
senses.why: The ordinal suffix -th attaches to eleven, marking one step past the tenth.
senses.whyCN: 序数后缀 -th 附加于 eleven，标记第十之后的又一步。

senses.title: One of eleven equal parts

senses.definitionCN: 整体分成十一等份中的一份。

senses.whyCN: 序数兼任分数名，eleventh 也指份额。

senses.title: The last possible moment

intro.en: Eleventh is eleven plus the old ordinal ending, with a famous idiom attached.
intro.cn: eleventh 是 eleven 加古老序数词尾，还挂着一条著名习语。

items.en: Old English endlefta formed the ordinal of endleofan.
items.cn: 古英语 endlefta 构成 endleofan 的序数形式。

items.en: Proto-Germanic ordinal patterns put the marker at the end.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语序数模式把标记放在词尾。

items.en: Middle English eleventhe smoothed into eleventh.
items.cn: 中古英语 eleventhe 简化为 eleventh。

items.en: Modern English keeps eleventh, notable for the n before th.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 eleventh，n 与 th 相接颇为独特。

items.en: The idiom the eleventh hour spread from an old vineyard parable.
items.cn: the eleventh hour 习语由一则古老葡萄园寓言传播开来。

note.en: Two compact groups: ordinal neighbors and the phrase family.
note.cn: 两组紧凑集合：相邻序数与习语家族。

normalIntro.cn: 五条联想，记住序数 eleventh。

normal.en: Eleventh keeps the n before th, unlike ten-tenth.

normal.en: An eleventh of a pie is a thin slice.

normal.en: Cricket innings can reach an eleventh round.

normal.en: Eleventh-hour news breaks just before deadline.
normal.cn: eleventh-hour 消息总在截稿前爆出。

abstract.cn: 想象钟在敲完十下之后再敲一下。

abstract.en: See a sprinter jumping in just before the flag falls.

abstract.en: Feel the th bite right after the soft n.

examples.cn: 救援在最后关头赶到。

examples.cn: 他们在最后一刻才签下协议。

examples.en: Each heir took an eleventh of the estate.
examples.cn: 每位继承人分得遗产的十一分之一。

sensesIntro.en: Eleventh ranks, divides, and crowns the famous last-hour idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: eleventh 排位、等分并顶起著名的最后时刻习语。

core.cn: 核心意象：十声钟响之后再敲的一下

intro.cn: eleventh 由数词加序数后缀并复合出习语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives remain scientific and legal counting words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族限于科学与法律计数词。

items.meaningCN: 构成序数的后缀（第十、第十二）

items.example: Peace talks began at the eleventh hour.

items.exampleCN: 最后一刻的扑救让球迷沸腾。

items.meaningCN: 截止时间——与 eleventh hour 相邻的概念

definition_en: in addition or different; or otherwise
core_image: 已选之外的那扇门：别的选项还开着
scene: 点餐台前他问同伴还要不要别的。Do you want anything else?
sceneCN: 这里 else 是「其他的东西」（第 1 个义项：另外的）；句意是你还要别的吗。图中可辨识物件：点餐台、菜单、两手空空的人、收银员。

pos.zh: 别的（用于疑问词、不定代词后）

senses.title: Different or additional
senses.definition: different from or in addition to the one mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 不同于已提到的，或在其之上另加的。
senses.example: Do you want anything else?
senses.exampleCN: 你还要别的吗？
senses.why: The old root means other, so else attaches to question words to open one more slot.
senses.whyCN: 古词根义为「别的」，else 挂在疑问词后即多开一个选项。

senses.title: Or otherwise, in warnings
senses.definition: used in or else to state what will happen if not
senses.definitionCN: 用于 or else，陈述不这样做的后果。
senses.example: Hurry up, or else we will miss the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们就赶不上车了。
senses.why: Two options fork here: comply or face the stated result.
senses.whyCN: 此处岔开两条路：照办，或面对陈述的后果。

senses.title: Someone other than a person
senses.definition: somebody other than the person concerned
senses.definitionCN: 所指的人之外的他人。
senses.example: Let someone else decide this.
senses.exampleCN: 让别的人来决定这件事。
senses.why: The word freely attaches to pronouns, making anyone into someone different.
senses.whyCN: 该词可自由附着于代词，把某人变成另一人。

intro.en: Else is the last living trace of an old word meaning other.
intro.cn: else 是古词「别的」在英语里的最后活痕迹。

items.en: Old English elles meant other, from ell, other, plus a genitive ending.
items.cn: 古英语 elles 意为别的，源于 ell（其他）加属格词尾。

items.en: Proto-Germanic aljas carried the other-idea across the family.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 aljas 把「其他」之义传遍语族。

items.en: Middle English elles lost its final s sound to become else.
items.cn: 中古英语 elles 失去词尾音素成为 else。

items.en: Modern English keeps else in questions, pronouns, and the or else threat.
items.cn: 现代英语的 else 活跃于疑问句、代词与 or else 威胁句。

items.en: Programming borrowed else for the other branch of an if decision.
items.cn: 编程语言借 else 表示条件判断的另一分支。

note.en: Else keeps close company with other-words and branch-words.
note.cn: else 与「其他」词和「分支」词关系紧密。

entries.definitionCN: 在别处——else 的复合词

entries.definition: one more of the same kind
entries.definitionCN: 另一个——补足选项的表达

normalIntro.en: Five hooks that keep else at hand.
normalIntro.cn: 五条联想，让 else 随手可及。

normal.en: Anything else is the shopkeeper's standard question.
normal.cn: anything else 是店员的标配问句。

normal.en: Or else hangs a quiet threat at sentence end.
normal.cn: or else 在句尾挂着一丝威胁。

normal.en: Elsewhere means in another place, two words fused.
normal.cn: elsewhere 即在别处，两词熔合。

normal.en: Programming uses if and else as twin branches.
normal.cn: 编程里 if 与 else 是孪生分支。

normal.en: Else follows question words like a loyal shadow.
normal.cn: else 像忠实影子跟随疑问词。

abstract.en: See one door chosen and many doors left open.
abstract.cn: 看见一扇门被选中，其余的门敞着。

abstract.en: Feel a fork where the unchosen path waits.
abstract.cn: 感受岔路口那条未被选之路在等待。

abstract.en: Hear a short dry syllable, like a quick tap.
abstract.cn: 听一个短促干涩的音节，像轻叩一下。

examples.cn: 你还要别的吗？

examples.en: Let someone else decide this.
examples.cn: 让别的人来决定这件事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱欧思」——「爱还有别的选项吗？或者思量一下」，谐音提示 else。

sensesIntro.en: Else opens extra options, adds threats with or else, and swaps people.
sensesIntro.cn: else 开出额外选项、以 or else 带威胁、并可换人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chosen door, many doors still open
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门已被选中，其余的门仍开着

intro.en: Else compounds with place and question words into everyday pairs.
intro.cn: else 与地点词、疑问词复合成日常搭配。

latinIntro.en: Latin-family entries supply the alternative-idea vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族提供「备选」概念的词汇。

definition_zh: 使尴尬；使窘迫；使局促不安
definition_en: to make someone feel awkward, ashamed, or uncomfortable in front of others
core_image: 当众卡壳的脸：脸一下子红了，手脚都不知道往哪放
scene: 生日会上朋友突然唱起了他五岁的糗事歌。The song embarrassed him in front of everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 embarrass 是「使尴尬」（第 1 个义项：使窘迫）；句意是那首歌让他在众人面前下不来台。图中可辨识物件：生日蛋糕、点歌的朋友、涨红的脸、捂脸的手。

senses.title: To make someone feel awkward
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel self-conscious or ashamed
senses.definitionCN: 使某人难为情或羞愧。
senses.example: The song embarrassed him in front of everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 那首歌让他在众人面前下不来台。
senses.why: The old sense meant to block or hamper, and social blockage becomes the blush of shame.
senses.whyCN: 旧义为阻碍，社交受阻便化为羞赧脸红。

senses.title: To hinder or complicate
senses.definition: to make a plan or person unable to act freely
senses.definitionCN: 使计划或人无法自由行动。
senses.example: Debt embarrassed the young company.
senses.exampleCN: 债务让这家年轻公司举步维艰。
senses.why: The literal French sense of blocking a road survives in financial and formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语「堵路」的本义保留于财经与正式文体。

senses.title: To involve in financial difficulty
senses.definition: to burden a person or business with trouble, especially money trouble
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或企业陷入困境，尤指财务困难。
senses.example: He was embarrassed by unpaid bills.
senses.exampleCN: 未付的账单让他捉襟见肘。
senses.why: When a road is blocked, resources stop flowing, so money troubles use the same image.
senses.whyCN: 路被堵则资源断流，财务困境沿用同一意象。

intro.en: Embarrass began as a road-blocking image in French and Spanish.
intro.cn: embarrass 起于法语与西班牙语「堵路」的意象。

items.en: Spanish embarazar meant to obstruct, and also to make pregnant, a curious double life.
items.cn: 西班牙语 embarazar 意为阻碍，也有「使怀孕」的奇特义项。

items.en: French embarrasser kept the blocking sense: to bar the way.
items.cn: 法语 embarrasser 保留阻碍义：拦住去路。

items.en: The word combines em-, in, with the Portuguese baraça, a halter or strap.
items.cn: 该词由 em-（入内）加葡萄牙语 baraça（笼头、皮带）构成。

items.en: English borrowed it in the seventeenth century with the hampering sense.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入，取其「妨碍」之义。

items.en: The social sense, to make someone blush, later became the dominant one.
items.cn: 「令人脸红」的社交义后来成为主导义项。

note.en: Two groups: spelling twins and the discomfort field.
note.cn: 两组：拼写孪生词与「不适」语义场。

entries.definitionCN: 大使馆——首音节相近，词源无关
拥抱——同为 em- 开头，义不同
可拥抱的——拼形易混
羞辱——程度更重的难堪
使蒙羞——书面色彩浓
羞愧的——embarrassed 的情绪结果

normalIntro.en: Five hooks that pin the blush of embarrass.
normalIntro.cn: 五条联想，钉住 embarrass 的脸红瞬间。

normal.en: Double r and double s: embarrass carries two r and two s.
normal.cn: 双 r 双 s：embarrass 里有两个 r 和两个 s。

normal.en: Em- plus bar: a bar blocking your way blocks your face into red.
normal.cn: em- 加 bar：拦路的横条把脸拦红。

normal.en: An embarrassing moment is a photo you wish did not exist.
normal.cn: 尴尬时刻是你希望不存在的照片。

normal.en: The embarrassment noun grows by adding -ment.
normal.cn: 名词 embarrassment 由加 -ment 构成。

normal.en: Debt embarrasses, an old financial use of the word.
normal.cn: 债务致困，是这个词的旧财经用法。

abstract.en: Picture a hot bar dropped across a doorway of faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一根发烫的横条砸在一排脸的门道口。

abstract.en: Feel cheeks warm and eyes hunting the exit.
abstract.cn: 感到双颊发热，眼睛急寻出口。

abstract.en: See two hands shielding a blushing face.
abstract.cn: 看见双手掩住发红的脸。

examples.en: The song embarrassed him in front of everyone.
examples.cn: 那首歌让他在众人面前下不来台。

examples.en: Debt embarrassed the young company.
examples.cn: 债务让这家年轻公司举步维艰。

examples.en: I felt embarrassed about forgetting her name.
examples.cn: 忘了她的名字，我感到很尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因巴若思」——「因为把路一拦，脸若火烧」，谐音串联 embarrass。

root: embarrass 来自法语 embarrasser（em- 入内 + 葡萄牙语 baraça 笼头），本义「加以阻碍」，引申为「使窘迫」。

sensesIntro.en: Embarrass moved from blocking roads to blocking faces into red.
sensesIntro.cn: embarrass 从堵路移情到把脸堵红。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar dropped across the way
core.cn: 核心意象：横条拦住去路

intro.en: Embarrass builds a full family with -ment and adjective forms.
intro.cn: embarrass 以 -ment 与形容词形式构成完整词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin-family words here share the in- or em- prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 此处拉丁词族共享 in-/em- 前缀。

definition_en: containing nothing; having no meaning or value; to remove everything from
core_image: 倒空后的瓶子：里面什么都没有
scene: 搬家那天纸箱一个个被搬空。She emptied the box onto the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 empty 是「倒空」（第 3 个义项：清空容器）；句意是她把箱子里的东西全倒在地板上。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、摊开的衣物、空荡的房间、卷起的胶带。

senses.title: Containing nothing
senses.definition: with nothing inside
senses.definitionCN: 内部没有任何东西。
senses.example: The hall was empty by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午时大厅已空无一人。
senses.why: A container without contents gives the concrete starting image.
senses.whyCN: 容器无物即得具体的起点意象。

senses.title: Without meaning or value
senses.definition: lacking real meaning, comfort, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真实意义、慰藉或目标。
senses.example: His apology rang empty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听来空洞。
senses.why: A hollow container promises much but holds nothing, so words and feelings reuse the image.
senses.whyCN: 空壳容器承诺满满却一无所有，言语与情绪便沿用此象。

senses.title: To remove everything from
senses.definition: to take all the contents out of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的所有内容取出来。
senses.example: She emptied the box onto the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把箱子里的东西全倒在地板上。
senses.why: The state becomes an action: making a container empty.
senses.whyCN: 状态转为动作：使容器变空。

intro.en: Empty grew out of an Old English phrase meaning quite free.
intro.cn: empty 出自古英语一个意为「完全空闲」的短语。

items.en: Old English aemtig came from aemetig, meaning at leisure, quite free.
items.cn: 古英语 aemtig 源于 aemetig，意为闲适、完全空出。

items.en: The root aemeti meant ease or leisure in the Germanic family.
items.cn: 词根 aemeti 在日耳曼语族中意为轻松、闲暇。

items.en: Middle English empti shifted the sense from free time to vacant space.
items.cn: 中古英语 empti 把义从空闲时间移向空缺空间。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective and adds the verb and plural noun uses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词并发展动词与复数名词用法。

items.en: Figurative uses about empty promises and empty feelings spread in modern writing.
items.cn: 关于 empty promises 与空虚感的比喻义在现代文本中铺开。

note.en: Two groups: sound neighbors and the nothing-inside field.
note.cn: 两组：音近词与「内部空无」语义场。

normalIntro.cn: 五条联想，走进 empty 的空壳世界。

normal.en: Empty has mp in the middle, like a drumbeat in a hollow room.
normal.cn: empty 中间有 mp，像空屋里的一声鼓点。

normal.en: Empties are bottles to return, the plural noun use.
normal.cn: empties 指待回收的空瓶，即复数名词用法。

normal.en: Run on empty means working without fuel left.
normal.cn: run on empty 指在燃料耗尽下硬撑。

normal.en: Empty promises promise much and hold nothing.

normal.en: The verb empties out boxes and minds alike.
normal.cn: 动词 empty 既倒空箱子，也倒空思绪。

abstract.cn: 倾斜瓶子，看着最后一滴离开。

abstract.en: Stand in a hall that echoes because no one is there.
abstract.cn: 站在因无人而回声四起的大厅。

abstract.en: Feel a chest with the air let out.
abstract.cn: 感受胸腔像被放光了气。

examples.en: She emptied the box onto the floor.
examples.cn: 她把箱子里的东西全倒在地板上。

examples.en: The hall was empty by noon.
examples.cn: 正午时大厅已空无一人。

examples.en: His apology rang empty.
examples.cn: 他的道歉听来空洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺普提」——「俺把东西全普提出去，就空了」，谐音提示 empty。

root: empty 来自古英语 aemtig（aemeti 空闲 + -ig 形容词尾），由「闲空」转指「空无一物」。

sensesIntro.en: Empty spans bare containers, hollow feelings, and the pouring-out action.
sensesIntro.cn: empty 覆盖空容器、空洞情感与倒空动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bottle tipped until nothing is left
core.cn: 核心意象：倒尽最后一滴的瓶子

intro.en: Empty compounds freely into everyday and idiomatic words.
intro.cn: empty 自由复合出日常与习语词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin-family words carry the formal vacant and void vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族承担正式的 vacant、void 词汇。

items.example: The emptiness of the desert awed us.
items.exampleCN: 沙漠的空旷令我们敬畏。

items.meaning: a space with nothing in it

items.example: She ran on empty for weeks.

definition_en: to give someone hope, courage, or reason to do something
core_image: 把手放在对方背上轻推：勇气被推着往前走
scene: 赛前更衣室里队长逐个拍过队友的肩。The captain encouraged every player before the match.
sceneCN: 这里 encourage 是「鼓励」（第 1 个义项：给人勇气）；句意是赛前队长鼓励了每一名队员。图中可辨识物件：更衣室、队服、搭肩的手、点头的队员。

senses.title: To give courage to someone
senses.definition: to make someone feel more confident and hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使某人更有信心和希望。
senses.example: The captain encouraged every player before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 赛前队长鼓励了每一名队员。
senses.why: The word literally means to put courage into someone, so the core is injecting bravery.
senses.whyCN: 该词字面即「把勇气注入某人」，核心是灌输胆气。

senses.title: To support or promote something
senses.definition: to help an activity grow by backing it
senses.definitionCN: 以支持促成某项活动的发展。
senses.example: The city encourages cycling with new lanes.
senses.exampleCN: 城市以新车道鼓励骑行。
senses.why: Backing a person generalizes into backing an activity or trend.
senses.whyCN: 支持某人泛化为支持某项活动或趋势。

senses.title: To make something bad more likely
senses.definition: to make it easier for something, often bad, to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某事更易发生，常指坏事。
senses.example: Long queues encourage ticket touting.
senses.exampleCN: 长队助长了黄牛倒票。
senses.why: The same push that lifts good actions can lift bad ones.
senses.whyCN: 同一股推力既能推动好事，也能助长坏事。

intro.en: Encourage is literally the putting of courage into a heart.
intro.cn: encourage 字面即「把勇气放进心里」。

items.en: Old French corage meant heart or inner spirit.
items.cn: 古法语 corage 意为心、内在精神。

items.en: French encourager meant to embolden, to put heart into.
items.cn: 法语 encourager 意为壮胆、鼓气。

items.en: The root goes to Latin cor, the heart, source of cordial too.
items.cn: 词根出自拉丁语 cor（心），cordial 亦出于此。

items.en: English borrowed encourage in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪借入 encourage。

items.en: Its negative twin discourage grew by swapping the prefix.
items.cn: 其否定孪生词 discourage 通过替换前缀产生。

note.en: Two groups: same-prefix verbs and the courage field.
note.cn: 两组：同前缀动词与「勇气」语义场。

entries.definition: to fill with a creative or heroic feeling
entries.definitionCN: 鼓舞；激励——偏精神感染

entries.definition: to give a reason to act
entries.definitionCN: 激励；促动——偏行为驱动

entries.definition: to make more cheerful and confident
entries.definitionCN: 振奋——courage 词根的同义回响

normal.en: En- plus courage: put courage in.
normal.cn: en- 加 courage：把勇气放进去。

normal.en: Discourage is encourage wearing a negative prefix.
normal.cn: discourage 是 encourage 换上否定前缀。

normal.en: An encouraging smile pushes a shy speaker forward.
normal.cn: 鼓励的微笑推着紧张的发言者向前。

normal.en: Long queues encourage bad habits, the dark side.
normal.cn: 长队助长坏习惯，是该词的阴暗面。

normal.en: Corage once meant heart itself in old French.
normal.cn: courage 在古法语里本指心。

abstract.en: Hear a steady drumbeat walking you ahead.

examples.en: The captain encouraged every player before the match.
examples.cn: 赛前队长鼓励了每一名队员。

examples.en: The city encourages cycling with new lanes.
examples.cn: 城市以新车道鼓励骑行。

examples.en: Long queues encourage ticket touting.
examples.cn: 长队助长了黄牛倒票。

definition_en: the last part of something; to finish; a purpose
core_image: 路的尽头：那条再往前就没有路的地方
scene: 书翻到最后一页，故事在这里画上句号。The movie ends with a quiet sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 end 是「结束」（第 3 个义项：完结）；句意是电影在安静的日出中结束。图中可辨识物件：黑屏字幕、初升的太阳、安静的海面、空座椅。

senses.title: The last part of something
senses.definition: the final part or point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的最后部分或端点。
senses.example: The movie ends with a quiet sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 电影在安静的日出中结束。
senses.why: A line has two tips, and this one names the far tip where things stop.
senses.whyCN: 线有两端，此义项指事物停止的那一端。

senses.title: A purpose or aim
senses.definition: the goal for which something is done
senses.definitionCN: 做某事所追求的目标。
senses.example: Winning votes was the only end of the speech.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得选票是这次演讲的唯一目的。
senses.why: The stopping point of an effort is also the target it aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 努力的终点同时就是它瞄准的靶心。

senses.title: To finish or bring to a stop
senses.definition: to stop or make something stop
senses.definitionCN: 停止或使某事停止。
senses.example: The meeting ended at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议于正午结束。
senses.why: The noun tip becomes a verb: to reach the stopping point.
senses.whyCN: 名词端点转为动词：抵达停止之点。

senses.title: A remaining piece or tip
senses.definition: a small piece left over, as in cigarette ends
senses.definitionCN: 剩下的小块，如烟蒂。
senses.example: Cigarette ends littered the pavement.
senses.exampleCN: 人行道上散落着烟蒂。
senses.why: What is cut off at the end is a tip itself, so leftovers get the same name.
senses.whyCN: 在末端被截下的东西就是端头，残余之物沿用此名。

intro.en: End is a native English word as old as the language itself.
intro.cn: end 是与英语同龄的本族词。

items.en: Old English ende named the tip, limit, or final point.
items.cn: 古英语 ende 指端点、界限或终点。

items.en: Proto-Germanic andazijaz, literally the opposite side, spread across the family.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 andazijaz，字面为「对侧」，传遍语族。

items.en: The purpose sense, end as goal, already lived in Old English texts.
items.cn: 「目的」义在古英语文献中已经存在。

items.en: Middle English ended the verb uses matured.
items.cn: 中古英语中动词用法成熟。

items.en: Modern English builds idioms like end up and make ends meet.
items.cn: 现代英语衍生 end up、make ends meet 等习语。

note.en: Two groups: same-root end words and the finish field.
note.cn: 两组：同根 end 词与「终结」语义场。

normal.en: End is as short as the last second of a race.
normal.cn: end 短如赛跑的最后一秒。

normal.en: Make ends meet is about joining two ends of money.
normal.cn: make ends meet 指让钱的两端接上。

normal.en: End up means where you finally land.
normal.cn: end up 指你最终落在哪里。

normal.en: The end of a rope frays into little threads.
normal.cn: 绳子的末端散成细丝。

normal.en: Endless adds less to mean without any end.
normal.cn: endless 加 less 表示无尽头。

abstract.cn: 沿路走到路面戛然而止处。

abstract.en: Hear a bell mark the last line of a chapter.
abstract.cn: 听钟声敲响一章的最后一行。

abstract.en: See a book close and the light go out.
abstract.cn: 看见书合上，灯熄灭。

definition_en: a person or force that hates or opposes another and tries to harm it
core_image: 隔着战壕对峙的那个人影
scene: 棋盘两侧棋子排成两军对垒之势。He studied his enemy's next move on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 enemy 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：敌对者）；句意是他在棋盘上琢磨对手的下一步。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、对坐的两人、推演的手、台灯。

senses.title: A person who opposes or hates
senses.definition: a person who feels hatred toward or seeks to harm someone
senses.definitionCN: 心怀仇恨或图谋伤害的人。
senses.example: He studied his enemy's next move on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他在棋盘上琢磨对手的下一步。
senses.why: The Latin root means not-friend, so the enemy is defined by hostile feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「非友」，敌人由敌意界定。

senses.title: Armed forces of the other side
senses.definition: the military forces of the opposing side
senses.definitionCN: 对方阵营的武装力量。
senses.example: The enemy advanced before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 敌军拂晓前推进。
senses.why: One hostile person expands to the whole hostile army.
senses.whyCN: 单个敌对者扩及整支敌军。

senses.title: Something harmful
senses.definition: a thing that damages or threatens something
senses.definitionCN: 损害或威胁某物的东西。
senses.example: Laziness is the enemy of progress.
senses.exampleCN: 懒惰是进步之敌。
senses.why: Anything that opposes a goal inherits the hostile image.
senses.whyCN: 凡阻碍目标之物皆承袭敌对意象。

intro.en: Enemy simply means the person who is not your friend.
intro.cn: enemy 的本义即「不是你朋友的人」。

items.en: Latin inimicus combines in-, not, with amicus, friend.
items.cn: 拉丁语 inimicus 由 in-（非）+ amicus（朋友）构成。

items.en: Old French enemi carried the word into medieval England.
items.cn: 古法语 enemi 把词带入中世纪英格兰。

items.en: Middle English enemi settled the spelling and the military sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 enemi 定型拼法并确立军事义。

items.en: Modern English keeps enemy for people, armies, and harmful forces.
items.cn: 现代英语的 enemy 用于人、军队与有害力量。

items.en: The related enmity keeps the abstract hostility meaning.
items.cn: 相关词 enmity 保留抽象的敌意义。

note.en: Two groups: the friend-opposite family and the opposition field.
note.cn: 两组：「友」之反义家族与「对抗」语义场。
